label: Docker Management Pro
summary: Advanced Docker/OCI workload lifecycle management: reviewed images/build provenance, scoped containers and application groups, private networks, ports, volumes, secret references, effective quotas, logs/health, coordinated updates and verified backups. Every exposed operation depends on an explicitly admitted provider and owned resource.
core_boundary: Essential native hosting, storage, isolation, permissions and any future qualified Docker/provider foundations remain open source. This module adds advanced workload orchestration through Core contracts; it never hands a tenant or package the host Docker socket, unrestricted daemon API, privileged containers, raw root commands or Core credentials.
acceptance: Qualify Docker/OCI versions and rootful/rootless assumptions, peer identity, cgroup delegation and actual CPU/RAM/PID/storage/log enforcement before declaring support.
Pin images to reviewed immutable digests with upstream source/license and provenance checks; isolate builds and refuse unreviewed image/build privileges.
Map tenant workload identity, UID/GID policy, allowed mounts, ports and network/egress ownership; refuse host sockets, sensitive bind mounts, host namespaces and unrestricted privileged modes.
Manage volume data, consistency boundaries, database dependencies, encryption/secret references and retention explicitly rather than treating container recreation as data recovery.
Bound logs, exec-like diagnostic capabilities, health checks and resource observations; module APIs cannot become arbitrary container or host command dispatch.
Exercise start/stop/update/drain and supported rollback with current authority, resource revisions, health evidence and per-workload outcomes.
Rehearse backup/restore of application data plus required configuration/secrets references on isolated targets; test failed pulls, full storage, daemon loss and interrupted updates.
On expiry/removal, stop new premium orchestration safely while containers, data, ordinary Core provider control and independent recovery remain available.
